title: Best time to buy and sell stock — one trade, unlimited, with a fee
label: ag-multi
statement: `prices[i]` is the price on day `i`. With **one** buy followed by **one** later sell, return the **maximum profit**, or 0 if no profit is possible.
provenance: A "stock buy/sell variation" was asked in a Staff Backend Bangkok loop (Oct 2025, codingkaro), and Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock scores 97.1% for Agoda on CodeJeet. Which variation was not reported, so the stages walk the standard ladder: one trade, unlimited, with a fee.

prompts.label: Check my design — no code
prompts.text: I believe one pass tracking the minimum price so far solves the single trade; for many trades, two running states — holding a share or not — capture every rule, including a fee per trade. Review my reasoning without giving me the implementation. What would break it?

prompts.label: Review, do not rewrite
prompts.text: Review my implementation for correctness and edge cases. Do not rewrite the code. List problems most severe first, each with the input that triggers it.

prompts.label: Race conditions
prompts.text: Now review this implementation for race conditions if multiple threads call MaxProfitOne concurrently. For each race, give the interleaving that breaks it. Then name the smallest synchronization boundary that preserves correctness. Do not write code yet.

prompts.label: Tests that expose bugs
prompts.text: Suggest tests that could expose bugs in my implementation: boundaries, duplicates, empty and invalid input, and concurrency where it applies. For each, say why the expected value is correct.

prompts.label: Complexity check
prompts.text: What is the time and space complexity of each public method as written? Do not claim a bound unless every step achieves it.

prompts.label: Requirement change
prompts.text: The requirement changed: Add Stock.MaxProfitUnlimited(prices) (long). List which members need to change and which do not, before writing any code.

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: `prices[i]` is the price on day `i`. With **one** buy followed by **one** later sell, return the **maximum profit**, or 0 if no profit is possible.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Must the sell come after the buy? (Yes.)
- Is no trade allowed? (Yes → 0.)
- Can profit exceed int with many trades? (Use long.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: For the single trade, the best sell today pairs with the lowest price seen before today — so remember the minimum, not every pair. For many trades, define what you hold at the end of each day and the transitions write themselves.

learn.title: 4 · Approach

learn.title: 11 · AI usage strategy
learn.md:
- Make the design decision yourself, then ask the assistant to attack it.
- Delegate the mechanical parts only after the structure is fixed.

**Prompts for this question:**

- *Check my design — no code* — "I believe one pass tracking the minimum price so far solves the single trade; for many trades, two running states — holding a share or not — capture every rule, including a fee per trade. Review my reasoning without giving me the implementation. What would break it?"
- *Review, do not rewrite* — "Review my implementation for correctness and edge cases. Do not rewrite the code. List problems most severe first, each with the input that triggers it."
- *Race conditions* — "Now review this implementation for race conditions if multiple threads call MaxProfitOne concurrently. For each race, give the interleaving that breaks it. Then name the smallest synchronization boundary that preserves correctness. Do not write code yet."
- *Tests that expose bugs* — "Suggest tests that could expose bugs in my implementation: boundaries, duplicates, empty and invalid input, and concurrency where it applies. For each, say why the expected value is correct."
- *Complexity check* — "What is the time and space complexity of each public method as written? Do not claim a bound unless every step achieves it."

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- O(n²) pairs.
- Allowing the sell before the buy.
- Charging the fee on both buy and sell.
- int overflow on unlimited-trade sums.
